disk.source: The mean of a study of the start on the cloud machine on 2026-11-21, with 23 samples of 5 s from /proc and /sys of the child. The child read 479 MiB by the age of 87 s (5.5 MiB/s). In its first 30 s it read 6 to 20 MiB in each 5 s with approximately 80 major faults each second, thus approximately 100 reads each second. The wait on the disk was 18 to 98 % of the CPU time, and the steal was 0.

cases.title: The start of alerts at the knee of the cloud log, on the disk of the cloud machine at the mean rate, with a cold cache and the other processes of the machine

observed.source: The file host/start-times.json of the cloud copy, read on 2026-11-21 at 18:3xZ: 20 good starts of 350cff5 from 2026-11-20 19:14:29Z to 2026-11-21 10:30:25Z, each one ready in the window of 90 s. The size of the log is the file of 18:44Z (197156864 B) times the share of the body characters up to the last good start (cb / b). Read: 2026-11-21T18:54:56Z to 18:56:01Z (65 s), on the cloud machine. The command was `timeout 180 nice -n 19 ionice -c3 /opt/node/bin/node`, with node:sqlite `DatabaseSync(<home>/runtime.sqlite, { readOnly: true })`. The exit code was 0. The query was one scan with the cut as a bound parameter, '2026-11-21T10:30:25.056Z' for both `?`: SELECT count(*) AS n, sum(length(body)) AS b, count(CASE WHEN at <= ? THEN 1 END) AS cn, sum(CASE WHEN at <= ? THEN length(body) END) AS cb FROM events Total: n = 145524 events, b = 158938576. Cut (at <= 10:30:25.056Z): cn = 141779 events, cb = 154047519. `at` is the ISO text of `toISOString()`, so the text comparison is a time comparison. `length(body)` counts characters, not bytes.
The supervisor of the cloud copy on 2026-11-21: 141 starts in a row by 18:44Z, each one stopped at the end of the ready window of 90 s. The stat of runtime.sqlite gave 197156864 B at 18:44Z.
